source_script.summary: In this Norse myth, Thor disguises himself as a bride to infiltrate a giant's palace and retrieve his stolen hammer, Mjölnir, from the giant Thrym.
source_script.narration: The mighty God of Thunder, Thor, faced a crisis when his magical hammer, Mjölnir, was stolen by a giant named Thrym. According to the supplied account, Thrym demanded to marry the goddess Freyja in exchange for the weapon, but she refused the giant's proposal. Loki devised a plan for Thor to dress as Freyja in a bridal gown and veil to infiltrate the giant's palace. Thor reluctantly agreed to the disguise and traveled to the giant's home to reclaim his property. During the wedding dinner, Thor consumed an entire ox, eight salmon, and three barrels of mead. Loki explained the bride's massive appetite by claiming she had not eaten for eight days due to wedding excitement. During the ceremony, Thrym ordered Mjölnir to be placed in the bride's lap to bless the union. Thor immediately grabbed the hammer, ripped off his disguise, and killed Thrym and the gathered giants. Thrym had spent days preparing for a wedding, but instead invited the God of Thunder to his own funeral.
